decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm elbow-up approach to the nearer left tube, keeping the right arm parked. Establish downward wrist orientation before final visual alignment.
Advance left wrist toward the tube nearest the rack while continuing the elbow-up downward approach; keep clearance until wrist-camera alignment is clearer.
Align above the near left tube with a small yaw adjustment to its axis. Descend only to a pregrasp height and inspect centering before closing.
Correct wrist-view alignment toward the tube body, lower slightly, then close the left gripper. Retention will be checked visually on a short lift.
Finish closing, then lift the first tube clear with a small retreat. Keep the wrist orientation fixed to verify the tube remains between the fingers.
Tube is retained in RGB. Begin rotating it upright while moving toward the rack, keeping it elevated and the left elbow-up branch continuous.
Continue the retained tube toward upright over a central rack opening. Keep the tube above the rack before the insertion descent.
Make the final small upright correction and lower cautiously toward the central opening. Use the next wrist view to check the tube-to-hole alignment.
Lower the upright tube in small increments, with a slight lateral correction toward the visible central opening. Keep grasp closed until it is seated.
Continue a slow vertical insertion and inspect for any tube motion relative to the fingers or contact at the rack before releasing.
The tube appears supported at the opening. Open the gripper in place, then withdraw slightly to inspect whether it remains upright and seated.
Withdraw open fingers from the rack and allow the released tube to settle. Its tilt is uncertain, so inspect the unobstructed rack before the next pickup.
Clear the rack to view the released tube, which appears tilted rather than seated. Keep both workspaces separated and prepare for a corrective pickup.
The released tube has fallen across the rack. First approach the unobstructed left tube from above; the fallen tube will need a separate corrective pickup.
Continue to a downward pregrasp above the remaining left-side tube, using a slow continuous wrist rotation.
Center the left tube in the wrist view and descend to grasp height without closing prematurely.
Make a small tube-axis correction, close around the centered body, and begin a short retention check.
Lift the second tube with a fixed wrist and closed gripper, checking retention before transporting it to an unblocked left rack slot.
Transport the visibly retained tube toward the left rack opening while gradually bringing it upright, maintaining clearance above the rack.
Continue rotating the held tube upright over the unblocked left side of the rack; keep it elevated for visual hole alignment.
Finish the upright rotation and position over a left-side large opening, accounting for the rack's current image location rather than the reference placement.
Lower toward the left-front large opening with a small rightward centering correction. Keep the tube upright and closed, inspecting contact before deeper insertion.
Continue vertically into the aligned left opening, retaining the tube until the insertion depth and support can be checked.
The tube moved upward relative to the fingers, indicating rim contact rather than a clean insertion. Lift clear and correct slightly left and away from the robot before trying again.
Increase clearance to expose the opening beneath the tube tip before another insertion attempt; the grasp has shifted and needs visual realignment.
Realign slightly farther over the opening, then descend with the shifted grasp still closed. Watch for tube slip rather than assuming low tracking error means insertion.
Test the corrected alignment with a slow vertical descent while monitoring the tube's position relative to the closed fingers.
The tube now descends without visible slip. Continue gently to seating depth, retaining the closed grasp until the next inspection.
Open in place to release the supported tube, then start withdrawing clear of the rack. Check that it remains upright after release.
The released left tube remains upright in its opening. Withdraw the left hand while starting an elbow-up approach to the loose right-side tube.
Move the right wrist toward its tube with a gradual downward, axis-aligned rotation; return the open left arm away from the rack without crossing workspaces.
Approach the right tube from above while aligning its long axis; leave the left arm near its origin with fingers open.
Complete right-tube axis alignment and lower to a pregrasp while the left hand finishes returning near origin.
Correct the right wrist toward the tube's cap and centerline, with a small yaw adjustment; do not close until the body is centered between the fingers.
Center the right tube between the fingers with a small forward adjustment, then close at grasp height. Keep the left arm parked.
Lift the right tube with the grasp fully closed and a fixed wrist orientation, checking retention before moving toward the rack.
Transport the retained right tube toward the rack and begin a gradual upright rotation, maintaining clearance and the right elbow-up configuration.
Continue the retained right tube toward the rack at clearance height, gradually rotating upright without changing grasp.
Bring the right tube upright above an empty right-side rack opening, keeping it clear of the seated tube and fallen central tube.
Center the right tube over the large right opening and descend cautiously. Keep the grasp closed and watch for rim contact or relative tube slip.
Lower the right tube vertically toward seating depth, monitoring its unchanged position in the fingers for evidence of a clear insertion.
Tube slip indicates rim contact. Lift clear and shift slightly right and toward the robot to better center the tube over the right-front opening.
Test the corrected right-slot alignment with a slow vertical descent, keeping the tube closed and watching for any further slipping against the rim.
The right tube now descends without visible slipping. Lower gently to seating depth before opening the gripper.
Release the right tube in place, then withdraw the open fingers slightly to check that the tube stays upright in the rack.
Both placed tubes remain upright. Clear the right hand and begin a left-arm approach to recover the remaining tube lying across the rack.
Approach the fallen tube from the left while turning the wrist to match its reversed cap direction. Return the right arm toward origin, retaining elbow-up continuity.
Continue the elevated recovery approach with a smooth wrist turn to the reversed tube axis; finish parking the right arm.
Move above the fallen tube while continuing the reversed-axis wrist alignment. Maintain height to avoid the two seated tubes.
Use smaller continuous wrist increments while moving to the fallen tube's centerline. Keep the gripper open and above the rack until axis alignment is visible.
The wrist turn was rejected at an angle wrap. Replan from the unchanged pose by unwinding toward the symmetric grasp orientation, keeping clearance above the rack.
